title: Thompson Vs. Bonfim Odds, Full Fight Preview & Prediction
text: Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) Welterweight talents Stephen Thompson vs. Gabriel Bonfim will go to war this weekend (Sat., June 28, 2025) at UFC Nashville inside Bridgestone Arena in Nashville, Tennessee. There is no doubt now that “Wonderboy” is in the twilight of his career. The 42-year-old Karate master is still a slick customer, but he’s grown a bit easier to track down with strikes and takedowns alike as the years continue to tick on by. Though he’s only lost to top talent, his back is unfortunately against the wall after losing four of five. Conversely, Bonfim is a very talented prospect 15 years his opponent’s junior. The Brazilian suffered a classic prospect loss to Nicholas Dalby in his third UFC appearance, but outside of that learning experience, he’s been very dominant in all aspects of the game, setting him up for a major opportunity here. Let’s take a closer look at the betting odds and strategic keys for each athlete: Thompson vs. Bonfim Betting Odds - Stephen Thompson victory: +310 - Stephen Thompson via TKO/KO/DQ: +900 - Stephen Thompson via submission: +3500 - Stephen Thompson via decision: +550 - Gabriel Bonfim victory: -395 - Gabriel Bonfim via TKO/KO/DQ: +550 - Gabriel Bonfim via submission: +125 - Gabriel Bonfim via decision: +200 - Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook How Thompson Wins “Wonderboy” is perhaps the best Karate representative in UFC history. He moves with great fluidity between stances, allowing him to control distance and score points with his kicks really well. He’s very good at suddenly covering that distance with his punches, and he’ll time hard counters as well. On the whole, this isn’t a terrible stylistic match up for Thompson. He’s fighter a jiu-jitsu ace with good wrestling and good Muay Thai, not an exceptional wrestler or frightening power puncher. If Thompson can keep his feet moving and deny the early takedown, he has a real shot here. It all comes down to cage position. Lately, Thompson has been easier to track down along the fence, and it gets him in trouble. From the first bell, his focus has to be on direction changes and intercepting shots up the middle, both of which will help buy him real estate and allow freedom of movement. As he showed versus Kevin Holland not too long ago, Thompson is still a very dangerous man if allowed to play his game. How Bonfim Wins Bonfim is quite experienced and skilled for his age. Perhaps most impressive, he transitions between all his skills nicely, using the threat of his kickboxing to set up his takedowns in a smooth fashion. Once on the canvas, Bonfim is clearly a top-notch grappler and has 13 wins via tapout to his credit. As mentioned above, this bout will be determined by location. If Bonfim is shooting at distance from Thompson’s kicking range, the takedown isn’t going to come, and he’s in for a rough night. Alternatively, if he’s able to back Thompson to the fence, hit him a time or two, then change levels, that submission prop is looking rather nice. A fast start seems wise here. We’ve seen Shavkat Rakhmonov, Belal Muhammad and Gilbert Burns wrangle Thompson by rushing him off the first bell. It’s become an increasingly easier option over the year as Thompson gets a little less sharp of a puncher and a little slower generally. Bonfim has the youth and stand up ability to get in Thompson’s face early, take a few punches if needed, and then get the wrestling going. Thompson vs. Bonfim Prediction A 15-year age difference is a hard statistic to overlook, particularly when Thompson was looking a bit worn down by 2021. Four years later, I’m not sure he has the grappling to resist such a talented black belt in jiu-jitsu. The margin for error is small, as Bonfim will start to dominate with even a single takedown, and Thompson just isn’t doing damage like he once did. There’s always a chance that vintage “Wonderboy” styles on his younger opponent — a la Holland, Vicente Luque and Geoff Neal — but the odds grow slimmer each year. title: UFC Fight Night – Stephen Thompson vs. Gabriel Bonfim: Preview & Betting Tips
text: Veteran Stephen “Wonderboy” Thompson faces off against surging Brazilian prospect Gabriel Bonfim in a welterweight bout between two fighters at the opposite end of their careers. Thompson (17-8-1), now 42, brings decades of elite-level striking experience into the Octagon and his resume speaks for itself. However, age is catching up and he’s coming off of two brutal losses and hasn’t shown the same spark that made him a top contender just a few years ago. Bonfim (17-1-0) may not be a household name yet, but he’s a serious threat in the welterweight division. The 27-year-old has quietly built a reputation as a finisher, particularly on the mat. He averages an impressive 3.68 takedowns per 15 minutes with 76% accuracy, and he stays busy on the ground with 2.2 submission attempts per fight. His footwork, timing, and accuracy made him a nightmare for reckless opponents. Nowadays though, the reflexes aren’t quite what they were, and Thompson’s weakness has always been grapplers who can pressure and chain takedowns. This is exactly what Bonfim will try to do. He’ll look to close the gap and suffocate the American veteran so that he cannot get off some of his sharp karate style of striking. And from there, he’ll look to initiate clinches and force the fight to the mat. In his younger days, Thompson would be able to evade a wrestler’s pressure by using lateral and vertical movement effortlessly. But, it just seems like a struggle now. And when this happens, it will tire you out more, which means as the fight goes on the wrestler will find more and more success. And I can see this happening in this one. This is a tricky fight for Stephen Thompson. While he remains one of the cleanest strikers in the division, his takedown defence has looked increasingly shaky, and age is a growing concern. Meanwhile, Bonfim is younger, hungrier, and thrives in exactly the kinds of situations where Thompson has historically struggled. Thompson’s days at the elite level certainly look to be behind him. And with a good performance and potentially a finish, the Brazilian would be taking a huge scalp here to elevate his own name and reputation. There isn’t much value in taking his moneyline, and with Thompson being stopped in his last two fights, unfortunately I’m willing to back him to make it three in a row. I’m taking Gabriel Bonfim to win by submission at odds of 2.55. And with a third successive stoppage loss, it pains me to say it, but we may see “Wonderboy” place his glove in the centre of the Octagon after the fight. Thompson, the current number twelve ranked welterweight contender, has been sidelined since UFC 307 back in October of last year, where he suffered a third round knockout loss against incoming headliner, Joaquin Buckley. As for Bonfirm, the 17-1 contender has suffered just a sole Octagon loss during his breif tenure, in the form of a knockout defeat to Nicolas Dalby. And last time out, Bonfirm secured a second round D’Arce choke submission win over Khaos Williams as recent as February. Stephen Thompson books UFC Nashville fight with Gabriel Bonfim UFC confirmed the return of Stephen Thompson against Gabriel Bonfim this evening on their official social media. Prior to his knockout loss to the surging, Buckley, Thompson had dropped a first round rear-naked choke submission loss to the unbeaten, Shavkat Rakhmonov — in his first submission blemish in combat sports to boot. Without a victory since 2022, on that occasion, Simpsonville native, Thompson had turned in an eventual corner stoppage TKO win over Kevin Holland in a main event clash at UFC Fight Night Orlando. For Bonfim, the highly-regarded welterweight contender is a product of Dana White’s Contender Series — and has racked up notable wins over the likes of the above-mentioned Williams, as well as Ange Loosa, Mounir Lazzez, and Trevin Giles. title: UFC Nashville staff picks include Tallison Teixeira to beat Derrick Lewis and more predictions
text: A clash of behemoths takes over Nashville as the UFC has booked Tallison Teixeira vs Derrick Lewis in the main event of their upcoming event. Derrick Lewis and Tallison Teixeira are headlining an intriguing card, booked just one week away from UFC 318, in Nashville, Tennessee. The UFC’s all-time knockout record holder will battle one of the biggest men in the UFC today, in what should be a titanic clash of epic proportions for fans to enjoy. Ahead of UFC Nashville, the experts at Bloody Elbow have made their staff picks for the two main event fights, as well as the Performance of the Night and the Fight of the Night. Derrick Lewis vs Tallison Teixeira predictions - Jordan Ellis – Tallison Teixeira - Kyle Dimond – Tallison Teixeira - James Sweetnam – Tallison Teixeira - Ross Markey – Tallison Teixeira The Bloody Elbow experts have made their staff picks for the upcoming UFC Nashville main event, and have unanimously chosen Teixeira to take home the win against a veteran of the octagon in Lewis. The undefeated Brazilian has only had one fight in the UFC so far, but it was an impressive one. Teixeira landed a 35-second knockout to overcome Justin Tafa at UFC 312, and will hope to do similar here in Nashville. However, it won’t be easy. Lewis has 23 knockout wins so far in his MMA career, although he has been very susceptible to defeat in the last few years. Of Lewis’s seven career losses, five have come in the last four years, showing that his best years are behind him. The fight with Teixeira could be a bout too far, and the experts fully expect the six-foot-seven-inch Brazilian to win this fight at UFC Nashville. Stephen Thompson vs Gabriel Bonfim predictions - Jordan Ellis – Stephen Thompson - Kyle Dimond – Stephen Thompson - James Sweetnam – Stephen Thompson - Ross Markey – Stephen Thompson The co-main event of UFC Nashville also has a clear favorite, as the Bloody Elbow experts all back Stephen Thompson to pick up the victory. While ‘Wonderboy’ may be in the last years of his career, the Karate master is still a force to be reckoned with. As one of the UFC’s oldest fighters at 42 years old, he will be looking towards retirement sooner rather than later after losing four of his last five bouts. However, Thompson’s losses have all come against top fighters in the division, and he even knocked out Kevin Holland in December 2022. Whether Gabriel Bonfim is a top talent or not has yet to be decided. While he has an impressive 17-1 record, he has not faced any big names in the UFC yet, with Thompson being his toughest test yet. UFC Nashville Fight of the Night - Jordan Ellis – Nate Landwehr vs Morgan Charriere - Kyle Dimond – Nate Landwehr vs Morgan Charriere - James Sweetnam – Junior Tafa vs Tuco Tokkos - Ross Markey – Nate Landwehr vs Morgan Charriere Three of the experts are looking forward to seeing Nate Landwehr vs Morgan Charriere, an undercard Featherweight fight which could be impressive in Nashville on Saturday. The two former champions have both earned numerous bonuses in the past for their exciting styles, giving this fight the chance to impress on an already exciting card. “The Last Pirate’s” last four wins have come via knockout, while Landwehr has only gone all three rounds once in his last four fights. However, James thinks that Junior Tafa against Tuco Tokkos has the potential to earn the Fight of the Night Bonus. Tafa is looking to improve on his mixed 2-3 record in the UFC so far, after picking up a win against Sean Sharaf to bounce back from two losses in a row. Meanwhile, his opponent is still searching for his first UFC win after failing to impress in his first two fights. This could be the last chance saloon for Tokkos, giving both men big motivation to give it their all in their fight. UFC Nashville Performance of the Night - Jordan Ellis – Vitor Petrino - Kyle Dimond – Steve Garcia - James Sweetnam – Vitor Petrino - Ross Markey – Steve Garcia The experts are split on who will pick up the Performance of the Night bonus, with two men in the running for the $50,000 bonus. Steve Garcia is backed by Kyle and Ross to impress in his Featherweight contest against Calvin Kattar on the main card. He is coming off five victories in a row, which included two performance of the night bonuses for epic first-round KO victories. His opponent has lost his last four fights, making the result of this fight seem more like a formality. He should easily dispatch Kattar and earn the Performance of the Night bonus if he can keep up his recent form. Meanwhile, both Jordan and James think that Vitor Petrino will finish Dejuan Lane to earn himself the cash prize for the best performance at UFC Nashville. The Brazilian started his UFC career well, but suffered back-to-back defeats in recent fights and will hope to bounce back convincingly against Dejuan Lane. He was knocked out by Mario Pinto back in March and could suffer the same fate at the hands of Petrino at UFC Nashville.

title: UFC Nashville preview: ‘Lewis vs. Teixeira’ main, co-main event predictions
text: Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) is just one day away from the upcoming UFC Nashville mixed martial arts (MMA) event, set to go down tomorrow night (Sat., July 12, 2025) on ESPN and ESPN+ at Bridgestone Arena in Nashville, Tennessee. UFC Nashville features a heavyweight main event between record-setting knockout artist Derrick Lewis and undefeated division prospect Tallison Teixeira, a five-round showdown with potential title implications for late 2025 and beyond. Before we dive into the main and co-main event, which includes the welterweight collision between former 170-pound title challenger Stephen Thompson and once-beaten Brazilian bruiser Gabriel Bonfim, check out Andrew Richardson’s “X-Factor” breakdown for the rest of the UFC Nashville main card by clicking here. Get all the latest “Lewis vs. Teixeira” odds and betting props courtesy of FanDuel right here. For UFC Nashville live results for this weekend’s fight card in the “The Volunteer State” click here. 265 lbs.: Derrick Lewis vs. Tallison Teixeira Derrick “The Black Beast” Lewis Record: 28-12, 1 NC | Age: 40 | Betting line: +210 Wins: 23 KO/TKO, 1 SUB, 4 DEC | Losses: 7 KO/TKO, 2 SUB, 3 DEC Height: 6’3” | Reach: 79” | Stance: Orthodox Significant Strikes Landed Per Minute: 2.48 | Striking accuracy: 50% Strikes Absorbed Per Minute: 2.48 | Striking Defense: 40% Takedown Average: 0.57 (26% accuracy) | Takedown Defense: 52% Current Ranking: No. 9 | Last fight: Technical knockout win over Rodrigo Nascimento Tallison “Xicao” Teixeira Record: 8-0 | Age: 25 | Betting line: -280 Wins: 7 KO/TKO, 1 SUB, 0 DEC | Losses: 0 KO/TKO, 0 SUB, 0 DEC Height: 6’7“ | Reach: 83” | Stance: Orthodox Significant Strikes Landed Per Minute: 14.61 | Striking accuracy: 59% Strikes Absorbed Per Minute: 7.50 | Striking Defense: 59% Takedown Average: 0.00 (0% accuracy) | Takedown Defense: 0% Current Ranking: No. 13 | Last fight: Technical knockout win over Justin Tafa Derrick Lewis has the most knockouts in the history of UFC and that’s probably the best thing you can say about the “Black Beast” in terms of his MMA career. To be fair, the 40 year-old Texan also has eight post-fight performance bonuses with three “Fight of the Night” honors, leaving him just one shy of the division mark set by former heavyweight champion, Stipe Miocic. Lewis has been competing for UFC since his technical knockout win over Jack May back in early 2014, a span of more than 11 years (Lewis was just 29 at the time of his debut). In the years that followed, “Mattress Mack’s” favorite customer compiled a record of 19-10 with one No Contest and he currently sits just inside the Top 10 at 265 pounds. Lewis has been dealing with a bad back for most of his career and has pretty much mailed it in for the last several years. “Black Beast” is coming off a technical knockout victory over Rodrigo Nascimento but has lost five of his last eight, getting finished in four of those losses. In fact, nine of his 12 losses have come by way of knockout or submission — but Lewis is rarely in a boring fight (this abomination notwithstanding). “I’ve fought way more tough fighters than this guy,” Lewis told UFC.com. “All his wins just came against guys that were 0-1, 1-2, 1-1, really having no experience. So they’re really trying to build this guy up for failure. That’s what I believe. I believe it’s too soon for him. That’s what I think. I believe there really are levels to it.” “I think coming up against a guy like me, very unpredictable, very dangerous, you never know what to expect,” Lewis continued. “I think it’s just too early for him to fight someone like me. He should expect that [I’m] going to come at him like no other opponent has come at him before. He’s going to realize that he made a big mistake signing that paper.” Tallison Teixeira is the new kid on the proverbial block and he’s already gotten everyone’s attention by racking up eight straight first-round knockout finishes. The Brazilian blasted his way onto the roster by popping and dropping Arthur Lopes on Dana White’s “Contender Series” back in Sept. of 2024 then followed that up with a 35-second finish over Justin Tafa at UFC 312. To earn a main event slot in just two fights for the promotion should tell you what matchmakers think of Teixeira’s skill set, or maybe they figure the aging and somewhat-brittle Lewis has declined enough to make this fight even, since they are not even remotely close in experience. Like most MMA fans, I like what I see from Teixeira and he is without question a lethal striker, Standing 6’7” with a 83-inch reach certainly helps, but not as much as fighting absolute nobodies on the international circuit. Lopes went back to the regional circuit after losing to Teixeira and Tafa is an undersized heavyweight, so I’m not sure those are the kinds of wins that should be driving “Xicao” to a -280 betting favorite. Did we already forget what happened to that other 6’7” heavyweight knockout artist who dazzled Dana White on “Contender Series” then won his first UFC fight by knockout? I’m talking about Robelis Despaigne, who went from cock of the walk to feather duster in two fights and is now fighting for those weird crypto bros under the Karate Combat banner. “I like this because I’ll be remembered as the man that ended the Brazilian curse,” Teixeira told MMA Fighting. “Brazilians need this after sad losses we had. Brazil needs this incentive, you know? I think that motivates me even more to give my best possible [performance] inside the Octagon.” Lewis is not without his issues and you can never quite tell if he actually gives a s—t about his fighting career or just wants to collect his paycheck and go home. What I can say for certain, is that he’s fought (and defeated) some of the best heavyweights in the world and also stopped heavyweights taller than Teixeira, like Alexander Volkov. Unless “The Black Beast” is completely washed (or completely checked out), I think he shows the 25 year-old hotshot there are levels to this game, even when some of the playing pieces are old and cracked. Prediction: Lewis def. Teixeira by knockout 170 lbs.: Stephen Thompson vs. Gabriel Bonfim Stephen “Wonderboy” Thompson Record: 17-8-1 | Age: 42 | Betting line: +320 Wins: 8 KO/TKO, 1 SUB, 8 DEC | Losses: 2 KO/TKO, 1 SUB, 5 DEC Height: 6’0“ | Reach: 75” | Stance: Orthodox Significant Strikes Landed Per Minute: 4.11 | Striking accuracy: 46% Strikes Absorbed Per Minute: 3.02 | Striking Defense: 55% Takedown Average: 0.25 (41% accuracy) | Takedown Defense: 63% Current Ranking: No. 12 | Last fight: Knockout loss to Joaquin Buckley Gabriel “Marretinha” Bonfim Record: 17-1 | Age: 27 | Betting line: -410 Wins: 3 KO/TKO, 13 SUB, 1 DEC | Losses: 1 KO/TKO, 0 SUB, 0 DEC Height: 6’1“ | Reach: 72” | Stance: Orthodox Significant Strikes Landed Per Minute: 5.22 | Striking accuracy: 43% Strikes Absorbed Per Minute: 3.80 | Striking Defense: 65% Takedown Average: 3.68 (76% accuracy) | Takedown Defense: 73% Current Ranking: Unranked | Last fight: Submission win over Kalinn Williams Stephen Thompson is 42 years old, has lost four of his last five, and is coming off a brutal knockout loss to Joaquin Buckley at UFC 307 last October. In fact, “Wonderboy” has just four wins over the last nine years but somehow retained his spot in the division Top 15, sandwiched between Geoff Neal and Carlos Prates. Thompson is a former kickboxer and continues to fight like one, getting taken down 17 times across his last five fights. I’m not sure what the former welterweight title challenger has left to offer at this point in his combat sports career, but trying to stay off the ground and outpoint fighters for a decision has not been a winning strategy and Thompson is facing an opponent who averages more than three takedowns per fight. “I’ve got two fights left, and we’re going to see them through, we’re going to honor them,” Thompson told MMA Junkie. “Go out there and win these next two fights in a great fashion, and we’ll see if we’ll keep going. It depends on what the UFC wants to do for sure. God forbid, if it doesn’t, then I’ve got other routes that I can take.” “I’m notorious for giving these guys a shot,” Thompson continued. “I did it with Vicente Luque, Geoff Neal, Kevin Holland. I’m just the guy to allow these guys to come up and test themselves. I wouldn’t be where I am if it wasn’t for those guys — Jake Ellenberger, Johny Hendricks, Rory MacDonald. Those guys gave me a shot. So just giving these guys a chance to prove themselves coming up, that’s kind of what it is at this point.” Gabriel Bonfim cut his teeth on Dana White’s “Contender Series” back in late 2022 and outside of his misstep against Nicholas Dalby the following year — when Bonfim was just 25 years old — the Brazilian has been virtually unstoppable, racking up four wins with three nasty finishes, two coming in the very first round. “Marretinha” may not be in his fighting prime just yet but he’s pretty damn close and already looks like a future title contender, though you can also argue that Bonfim has yet to fight an elite welterweight. I doubt anyone is breaking out the party hats for victories over Kalinn Williams and Ange Loosa. Stylistically, this is simply a bad matchup for Thompson, who thrives when opponents afford him the space to strike from range, like Kevin Holland. Despite his numerous submissions, Bonfim is no slouch on his feet and will be able to keep “Wonderboy” in reverse with his constant aggression. That should lead to some tie-ups against the cage and eventually, the takedown. Thompson has only been submitted once in his professional MMA career, though it’s probably because he’s never fought a black belt in Brazilian Jiu Jitsu with the credentials of Bonfim. I don’t want to harp on the age difference here (it’s 15 years if you’re counting) so I will instead harp on the fact that Thompson continues to look worse in each successive fight. title: UFC Stephen Thompson vs Gabriel Bonfim: Prediction and Breakdown - Sidekick Boxing
text: Stephen “Wonderboy” Thompson returns to action on July 12, 2025, at the Bridgestone Arena in Nashville, Tennessee, facing unbeaten Brazilian Gabriel Bonfim. It’s a compelling clash of styles: Thompson’s veteran striking and range control versus Bonfim’s youthful power and submission skill. With contrasting career trajectories and skill sets, this matchup could turn on simple physics—who can impose their game plan first. Tale of the Tape | Fighter | Stephen Thompson | Gabriel Bonfim | |---|---|---| | Record | 17–8–1 | 17–1 | | Age | 42 | 27 | | Height | 6’0″ | 6’1″ | | Reach | 75″ | 72½” | | Stance | Orthodox (karate base) | Orthodox | Analysis Stephen Thompson remains among MMA’s most elusive and technical strikers, even at 42. His karate-influenced stance, lateral movement, and volume of kicks allow him to dictate distance and tempo. Against forward-charging opponents, he has repeatedly shown his ability to pick spots, counter effectively, and avoid damage. SHOP: The Kickboxer Collection Gabriel Bonfim comes in as a stark contrast—undefeated, aggressive, and submission-focused. He’s finished nearly every fight, often rapidly via guillotine or choke. But his offensive style is linear; he tends to overcommit when closing distance, which creates openings for counterstrikers. And while his grappling is dangerous, it’s yet to be tested against someone as defensively sharp as Thompson. The fight hinges on whether Bonfim can close the gap without walking into counters. Thompson’s takedown defense and footwork can frustrate and neutralize less disciplined pressure. If Thompson stays light on his feet and lands crisp counters, he’s likely to frustrate Bonfim out of his rhythm and gradually take control. Prediction Expect early grappling attempts from Bonfim, but if he fails to score a takedown or mix up levels quickly, he’ll play into Thompson’s strengths. The veteran’s timing and accuracy should enable him to catch Bonfim charging in with a clean shot. Thompson’s experience and movement advantage are key. Expect him to manage distance, land decisive counters, and potentially force a stoppage—unless Bonfim dramatically improves his entry discipline or submission timing. Tallison Teixeira Derrick Lewis (28-12-0-1) is the No. 9 fighter in the official UFC heavyweight rankings. The 40-year-old former UFC title challenger is coming off a May 2024 knockout win over Rodrigo Nascimento. Lewis, who owns the record for most knockouts in UFC history with 15, is 2-4 in his past six trips to the Octagon dating back to February 2022. Lewis has been with the UFC since 2014. He also has the UFC record for most finishes in the heavyweight division with 15. No active UFC heavyweight has as many fights in the Octagon as Lewis does at 29. Lewis has a UFC heavyweight record eight fight-night bonus awards. Tallison Teixeira (8-0) joined the UFC in 2024 with a knockout win on a Dana White Contender Series card. The 25-year-old made his official UFC debut in February 2025, scoring a first-round knockout, and a “Performance of the Night” bonus in a win over Justin Tafa. The UFC is wasting no time in throwing Teixeira into the deep end of the heavyweight pool, giving him a veteran opponent in a main event contest. All eight of Teixeira’s career wins have come via first-round stoppage (seven knockouts, on submission). He has been a pro since 2021. He is ranked No. 13 in the UFC’s heavyweight weight class. When the opening betting odds were first published for Lewis vs. Teixeira, Teixeira opened as the -200 betting favorite over the +165 Lewis. The betting line has shifted. Today, Teixeira is -300 to Lewis’s +240. Lewis has picked up 72 percent of the bets on the UFC Nashville main event, but Teixeira has 71 percent of the handle. If you’re looking for an outcome for Lewis vs. Teixeira, I’d say lean toward the fight ending via knockout, and maybe even a first round knockout. My expectation is that the veteran who has been in the Octagon against some of the heaviest hitters in the UFC’s heavyweight division is going to be anxious to test the young man who only has 35 seconds of UFC fight time to his name. We don’t know much about Teixeira outside of the fact that he’s bigger and younger than Lewis. And while this matchup won’t answer every question we have about Teixeira, it should tell us if he is able to use his size and reach as well as take a punch from the UFC’s all-time leader in knockouts. The big concern is Teixeira’s defense. He can get tagged and tagged clean. That is an enormous concern. In an ideal world, Teixeira uses his length to use his kicks to hurt Lewis to the body and then finish him when Lewis is hurt. title: UFC Nashville odds: Best betting props, parlays and picks | Lewis vs. Teixeira
text: UFC Nashville goes down this weekend (Sat., July 12, 2025) inside Bridgestone Arena in Nashville, Tennessee. The main event features Heavyweights with Derrick Lewis vs. Tallison Teixeira. Lewis, a divisional stalwart, is hoping to get past the UFC neophyte and secure a fight with new UFC champion, Tom Aspinall. When it comes to the rest of the UFC Nashville card, there’s not too much to write home about. The co-main is Stephen Thompson vs. Gabriel Bonfim. Rounding out the main card is Calvin Kattar vs. Steve Garcia, Nate Landwehr vs. Morgan Charriere, Vitor Petrino vs. Austin Lane and Junior Tafa vs Tuco Tokkos. UFC Nashville’s “Prelims” are headlined by Max Griffin vs. Chris Curtis. The “Prelims” also have Jake Matthews vs. Chidi Njokuani and Lauren Murphy vs. Eduarda Moura. As always, there’s lots to bet on this card and we’ve got odds for all the fights below: UFC Nashville Main Card Money Line Odds Derrick Lewis (+220) vs. Tallison Teixeira (-270) The towering Teixeira is just 8-0 and two fights into his UFC career. He debuted in the Octagon with a Contender Series first round knockout over Arthur Lopes. In his proper debut, he put away Justin Tafa in 35 seconds (see it here). Lewis — who turned 40 this year — is coming off a third round technical knockout win over Rodrigo Nascimento. Before that, he lost a five-round decision to Jailton Almeida. And before that, he scored a 33-second win over Marcos Rogerio Lima (see it here). That win snapped a three fight losing skid (all finishes) where he lost to Serghei Spivac, Sergei Pavlovich and Tai Tuivasa. There’s not much to scout when it comes to Teixeira. He’s very tall and very long and he’s coming into UFC in his athletic prime at only 25 years-old. Lewis is giving up four inches of height and four inches of reach to the young Brazilian. The last time Lewis fought someone with that kind of reach it was Pavlovich and he lasted just 55 seconds. Lewis is capable of the spectacular and shocking in an Octagon. But, it really feels like the odds are stacked against him here, with a fighter so long, so powerful and with so much youth on his side. Lewis’ defense against significant strikes is just 40 percent. That spells a lot of trouble for “The Black Beast” against a man who, so far, has landed 14.61 significant strikes per-minute across his three Octagon appearances. In Heavyweight, it only takes one punch to win, a lot of the times, but I have to favor the man who is going to be landing dozens of them in a round (if it makes it that far). The round total for this fight is set at 1.5. I think the under is most likely, as do many others. The odds are just -210 for that prop. Teixeira by KO/TKO/DQ is a laughable -185. And Teixeira to win by strikes in round one is just -125. Clearly, there’s not much value if you believe Teixeira is going to quickly separate Lewis from his consciousness (as I do). For my best bet, I’m going to go for a winning round and method of victory parlay. I’m taking round one and TKO/KO/DQ. This covers me just in case Lewis does something silly/outstanding in the first round in Nashville. Best bet: Fight to end in Round 1 by KO/TKO/DQ (-150) Stephen Thompson (+320) vs. Gabriel Bonfim (-410) Thompson is coming off a third round knockout loss to Joaquin Buckley (see it here). Before that, he was submitted by Shavkat Rakhmonov (see it here). His last win was over Kevin Holland, when Holland retired at the end of round four. Bonfim, on the other hand, choked out Khaos Williams in his last fight (see it here). Before that, he took a decision over Ange Loosa. Before those fights he lost, as a big favorite, to Nicolas Dalby via technical knockout (see it here). I don’t think Thompson is long for this sport. He turned 42 this year and his fighting style isn’t great for masking your age. He can’t hide behind takedowns and take dangerous finishers out of their comfort zones. He has to stand in front of them and hope he can slip strikes and land enough from range to earn a decision. Bonfim is not a dangerous striker, so I’m not worried about Thompson getting KO’d for the second time in two fights. Bonfim’s submission threat is what I’m worried about, though. Bonfim’s submissions come from all angles and at a scary pace. I don’t think Thompson will be able to fight those off for long enough to stay in the fight and will probably end up tapping from a choke. Thompson has never had elite takedown defense. With age, his 63 percent takedown defense will feel closer to 50 percent. Bonfim lands almost four takedowns per 15 minutes. He’s going to get Thompson down. Bonfim by submission is only +125. I feel strongly that this is what’s going to happen. But those odds are a little stingy. Unfortunately, the Bonfim -3.5 is even stingier at -205. For my best bet I’m going deep into DraftKings props and I’m looking at Bonfim to win in rounds one or two. I really struggle to see Thompson make it to the final bell and this at least covers me if Thompson is shot to the point that Bonfim can get him out of there with ground-and-pound. Best bet: Gabriel Bonfim to win in rounds 1-2 (+120) Calvin Kattar (+102) vs. Steve Garcia (-122) The Featherweight division have a right to be scared of Garcia. He’s one a five-fight finish streak right now, including stoppages over Melquizael Costa (see it here) and Chase Hooper (see it here). Hooper and Costa have looked pretty good since then, so that tells us what kind of level Costa has been operating at lately. Kattar, on the other hand, will lock up a rare five-fight losing streak in UFC if he gets stopped by Garcia. Last time out he was well beaten by Youssef Zalal (who won despite staying in cruise control). Before that, he was beaten by Aljamain Sterling, Arnold Allen (due to an injury) and Josh Emmett (split decision). Kattar’s toughness is the stuff of legend, thanks to the unholy beating he once took from Max Holloway. Kattar has never been stopped in his career (other than that knee injury). At 37, though, with all these wars in his past, is this the time we see that chin fade? I think so. Garcia’s punches land like a sock full of pennies. And I fear he’s going to land something really hard on Kattar. I think we’re going to see a technical knockout from Garcia, probably from ground-and-pound. I’ll take the point spread here on Garcia, believing that if Kattar doesn’t go down, Garcia will still take a dominant decision (also because Garcia by KO was only +165). Best bet: Steve Garcia -3.5 (+110) Nate Landwehr (+220) vs. Morgan Charriere (-270) Landwehr got styled on in his last fight. Doo Ho Choi looked incredible as he out-struck and out-wrestled and eventually finished “The Train” (see it here). Before that, Landwehr scored a comeback technical knockout on Jamall Emmers (see it here). In his early UFC career, Landwehr managed to get wins over Darren Elkins, L’udovit Klein and David Onama. Charriere, meanwhile, is coming off a unanimous decision loss to Nathaniel Wood where he looked good, not great. Before that, he blew away Gabriel Miranda with a left hook (see it here). Landwehr is a hard-nosed brawler who is willing to eat two shot to land one. He’s a bit like Elkins without the grappling (as exposed by how often Choi took and held him down). I think this is a very tough match-up for him, against Charriere who has looked good against opponents who charge at him. Both these guys absorb more significant strikes than they land (which is a big red flag for me), but Charriere’s negative differential is higher. Charriere is also giving up three inches in the reach department. Even so, I think Charriere’s counter punching will be the story of this fight. Landwehr doesn’t exactly fight behind his jab and pick his shots. He’ll be crashing forward trying to overwhelm Charriere. In this situation, I like Charriere to respond with something hard that puts Landwehr down. Charriere reminds me of a striker in football/soccer who misses the goal when he’s given too much time to think about his shot, but who can score on instinct when the ball comes to him and he has to react without thinking. That’s how I see Charriere getting his finish here. Best bet: Morgan Charriere moneyline (-220) Vitor Petrino (-700) vs. Austen Lane (+500) Petrino’s shiny 11-0 record was dulled by Anthony Smith and Dustin Jacoby last year. Smith scored a quick guillotine on the Brazilian (see it here) in Brazil. Then Jacoby scored a late knockout in a very boring fight (see it here). Lane, meanwhile, was KO’d by Mario Pinto last time out (see it here). Before that, he successfully fraud checked Robelis Despaigne. Prior to that fight, he was starched by Jhonata Diniz (see it here). If it wasn’t for Tuco Tokkos, Lane might be the worst fighter on a UFC main card this year. Lane has a terrible 40 percent defense on significant strikes. That’s a death sentence at Heavyweight. For the most part in his career, big shots have been able to find Lane and he’s been stopped more than your average bear (all six of his defeats are by knockout). He’s been stopped so much, that you wonder whether the 37 year old should still get a license. But, this is MMA, right? We’ll let anyone fight. Petrino came to UFC with a reputation for vicious striking, but we’ve not seen much of that in the Octagon. What we have seen has been pretty slow and telegraphed. Is that still too fast and unpredictable for Lane, though? Lane has a decent-size advantage against Petrino and I can actually see him taking Petrino down and laying on him for a round or two. However, whenever they are standing I’m worried that Lane is one punch away from being laid out. This is what we saw in the Diniz fight. Since they start rounds standing, I have to give this to Petrino. I’m not very enthusiastic about the pick, though. The round total is 1.5. I’ll go with the over, thinking Lane will get his early takedown and Petrino will continue to underwhelm, even in a winning effort. Best bet: Over 1.5 rounds (+135) Junior Tafa (-166) vs. Tuco Tokkos (+140) Tafa put away super short notice opponent Sean Sharaf back in Oct. 2024. That was his first fight since being heel hooked by Valter Walker (who fights further down the card). Before that, Tafa was TKO’d by Marcos Rogerio de Lima (see it here). Tokkos, meanwhile, stifled Navajo Stirling last time out, losing just by decision to the super hyped prospect. Before that he was submitted by Oumar Sy, with Sy locking up the rear-naked choke when Tokkos was mugging for the commentary booth. Tokkos, as referenced earlier, is probably the worst main card fighter of the year. He’s not shown us much of anything thus far in his UFC career. He did well to hang in there against Stirling, but he offered very little offensive threat. Stirling’s passivity was mostly to blame for that awful fight going the distance. Tafa isn’t much better. He’s 2-3 in UFC and the two guys he beat are well below UFC quality. I think Tafa wins this, thanks to how hittable Tokkos is (4.99 significant strikes absorbed per minute and just 33 percent significant strike defense). I wouldn’t be surprised if we get another stinker, though, that goes the distance with a decision that could go to either guy. Because I’m not sold on Tafa, over 1.5 rounds looks quite appealing. Best bet: Over 1.5 rounds (+105) UFC Nashville ‘Prelims’ Under Card Odds Max Griffin (+250) vs. Chris Curtis (-310) This is our featured “Prelim”? I guess this slot really is just, “the fight before the main card” now. The 39-year-old Griffin was tapped by Michael Chiesa in Dec. 2024. He’s been win-loss-win-loss for the past few years, with the wins being split decisions over Jeremiah Wells and Tim Means. The 37-year-old Curtis is coming off trying to separate Sean Strickland from some dude in a regional MMA cage. In his last UFC fight, Curtis lost a controversial fight with Roman Kopylov (see it here). That fight was officially ruled a head kick knockout loss at 4:59 of round three. Many felt the fight could have been left for the remaining second and then have the judges decide (I scored it for Kopylov anyways). Griffin is an okay striker and wrestler, but at 39, his potency in either area needs to be questioned. Curtis, who isn’t much younger, seems to still be a reliable and creative volume striker. His very good takedown defense probably holds up to the level needed to stay up against Griffin, too. I think there’s a chance Curtis gets a stoppage in this fight, but it might come late. I’m not going to mess around with any round betting here and instead just go with Curtis on the moneyline. Best bet: Chris Curtis moneyline (-310) Jake Matthews (+124) vs. Chidi Njokuani (-148) Both these guys are on good runs and coming off decisive wins. It’s a little surprising to see them matched up here on the “Prelims.” Matthews beat Francisco Prado by unanimous decision in February. Last year, he defeated Phil Rowe. Prior to that, he managed to make it to a losing decision against the undefeated Michael Morales. Njokuani, meanwhile, lit up Elizeu Zaleski dos Santos on the co-main of an APEX card in March (see it here). He did miss weight for that one, though. Prior to that TKO he beat Jared Gooden and Rhys McKee. Njokuani is very big for the weight class. He’s four inches taller than Matthews and will have a long seven-inch reach advantage. That reach could be significant, as it was in Njokuani’s destruction of Dos Santos. Njokuani’s reach gets even more deadlier when you consider he has the best accuracy rate for sig. strikes in the division at 62 percent. The only reason he isn’t the official leader in that stat at Welterweight is because his last two fights have technically been Catchweights (due to his weigh-in misses). The 62 percent is better than Gunnar Nelson’s official best mark of 60.6 percent and all the other killers in this rejuvenated weight class. Matthews is no slouch, though. He’s an intelligent and well rounded fighter. He probably knows he can’t win a kickboxing match and I think he’s going to try and make this an ugly brawl against the fence. He’ll look to grind on Njokuani and land a few takedowns. That might be tough, though, given Njokuani’s 75 percent takedown defense. Ultimately, I think Njokuani is going to prevent himself getting taken down in this fight. And, if Matthews, won’t let him strike from range, I still think Njokuani has a good shot at landing heavy strikes right inside Matthews’ kitchen. Njokuani’s Muay Thai style is perfect for clinch fighting, so he might find a home for some good elbows and knees. The round total for this one is set at 1.5 for some reason. The over on that is -298, so no value there. And I don’t think there’s a finish in this fight. I’ll just go with the Njokuani moneyline. Best bet: Chidi Njokuani moneyline (-148) Lauren Murphy (+440) vs. Eduarda Moura (-600) Murphy has been out of action since her bruising loss to Jessica Andrade in Jan. 2023. Before that, she dominated the un-retired Miesha Tate. Before those fights, she was TKO’d while trying to get the belt off Valentina Shevchenko. Moura, meanwhile, took a decision over Veronica Hardy in her Flyweight debut last year. That fight came after she misses weight in back-to-back Strawweight bouts. I get that Murphy has been out awhile, and that she’s 42, but Vegas is showing a lot of faith in Moura with these lines. Despite her age and inactivity as of late, I bet Murphy still “has that dog in her” and I think she will bring a lot of pressure to Moura. Moura has managed to package together wins thanks to her takedowns. Murphy’s takedown defense has been solid over her career (69 percent). The big question is whether Murphy still has good takedown defense or not. If she keeps this fight standing I think she has a good chance to take a close decision. If she is taken down, I think Moura should be able to keep her down and get a pretty comfortable decision. Either way, I think we’re going to decision. Best bet: Over 2.5 rounds (-330) Kennedy Nzechukwu (-205) vs. Valter Walker (+170) Nzechukwu is undefeated (2-0) in UFC’s Heavyweight division. In Dec. 2024, he scored a first round technical knockout over Lukasz Brzeski (see it here). Walker, on the other hand, lost to Brzeski, by decision, in his UFC debut. Since then he’s heel hooked both Junior Tafa (who didn’t like it one bit) and Don’Tale Mayes. Nzechukwu’s striking should be too much for Walker to handle. However, Nzechukwu is a little ungainly and I can totally see him getting caught by Walker’s leg locks, perhaps even after scoring a knockdown. This match-up really seems ripe for some Heavyweight nuttiness. I think it’s best to play the under in this situation, especially with the round total set at 2.5 (I was sure it would be 1.5). Best bet: Under 2.5 rounds (-105) Mitch Ramirez (+700) vs. Mike Davis (-1000) Ramirez was stopped by Thiago Moises leg kicks in his last fight (see those here). His only other Octagon appearance was a walloping from Carlos Prates on Contender Series. In the opposite corner, Davis returned from a year long lay-off to fight Fares Ziam in February. He looked out of sorts and was possibly carrying an injury in that fight. He seemed to be trying to minimize damage more so than win a fight. That unanimous decision was his first UFC loss since being submitted by Gilbert Burns in 2019. He’s won four UFC fights between those losses. If the Davis we’re used to seeing shows up, then he should win this without too much trouble (as reflected in those betting lines). I think we’ll see the good version of Davis in this fight and if that happens, then his funky grappling should lead to a convincing win, probably by stoppage. Best bet: Under 2.5 rounds (-180) Fatima Kline (-1200) vs. Melissa Martinez (+750) Kline was fed to the wolves on her UFC debut, coming in on short notice and up a weight class to take on Jasmine Jasudavicius. She got dominated by the bigger fighter in that bout, but rebounded with a technical knockout over Victoria Dudakova (see it here). Prior to joining UFC, Kline was a champ in the CFFC organization. She also has BJJ black belt under Mike Wacker. Martinez, meanwhile, is 1-1 in UFC with a decision win over Alice Ardelean and a decision loss to Elise Reed. She’s a former champ in the Combate organization. Martinez — who is just 5’2” — should be fighting at Atomweight (and UFC should have an Atomweight division). Kline is going to have a lot of size and strength over her (not much reach, though). I think that size difference will be most notable on the ground and I think Kline is going to use that to get a submission. Best bet: Under 2.5 rounds (+114) UFC Nashville Long Shots! Here’s a couple of long shots for Saturday night’s action. Derrick Lewis to Win and Over 3.5 (+1000) Let’s just imagine that Teixeira is being over-hyped and that his best work has all come against tomato cans. And let’s imagine that Lewis is going to rewind the clock and survive a lot of early punishment. Maybe Teixeira punches himself out? And then, maybe Lewis uncorks one of his classic right hooks that knocks him out cold? It’s not impossible, right? It’s Heavyweight after all. Three-fight parlay: Tallison Teixeira, Steve Garcia, Valter Walker (+568) Despite that first long shot bet, I’m reasonably confident that Teixeira is legit enough to be better than a 40-year-old Lewis. I’m also pretty confident that Steve Garcia will add to his impressive winning streak when he meets Kattar. Walker is my wild card in this parlay and he’s here to add some value. Nzechukwu has looked good at Heavyweight so far, but he’s not faced anyone like Walker. Morgan Charriere to win by KO/TKO/DQ and over 1.5 rounds (+550) I used DraftKings to make my own same game parlay here. It kind of kills me to do it, since I really like Landwehr. title: UFC Nashville preview: ‘Lewis vs. Teixeira’ main, co-main event predictions
text: Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) is just one day away from the upcoming UFC Nashville mixed martial arts (MMA) event, set to go down tomorrow night (Sat., July 12, 2025) on ESPN and ESPN+ at Bridgestone Arena in Nashville, Tennessee. UFC Nashville features a heavyweight main event between record-setting knockout artist Derrick Lewis and undefeated division prospect Tallison Teixeira, a five-round showdown with potential title implications for late 2025 and beyond. Before we dive into the main and co-main event, which includes the welterweight collision between former 170-pound title challenger Stephen Thompson and once-beaten Brazilian bruiser Gabriel Bonfim, check out Andrew Richardson’s “X-Factor” breakdown for the rest of the UFC Nashville main card by clicking here. Get all the latest “Lewis vs. Teixeira” odds and betting props courtesy of FanDuel right here. For UFC Nashville live results for this weekend’s fight card in the “The Volunteer State” click here. 265 lbs.: Derrick Lewis vs. Tallison Teixeira Derrick “The Black Beast” Lewis Record: 28-12, 1 NC | Age: 40 | Betting line: +210 Wins: 23 KO/TKO, 1 SUB, 4 DEC | Losses: 7 KO/TKO, 2 SUB, 3 DEC Height: 6’3” | Reach: 79” | Stance: Orthodox Significant Strikes Landed Per Minute: 2.48 | Striking accuracy: 50% Strikes Absorbed Per Minute: 2.48 | Striking Defense: 40% Takedown Average: 0.57 (26% accuracy) | Takedown Defense: 52% Current Ranking: No. 9 | Last fight: Technical knockout win over Rodrigo Nascimento Tallison “Xicao” Teixeira Record: 8-0 | Age: 25 | Betting line: -280 Wins: 7 KO/TKO, 1 SUB, 0 DEC | Losses: 0 KO/TKO, 0 SUB, 0 DEC Height: 6’7“ | Reach: 83” | Stance: Orthodox Significant Strikes Landed Per Minute: 14.61 | Striking accuracy: 59% Strikes Absorbed Per Minute: 7.50 | Striking Defense: 59% Takedown Average: 0.00 (0% accuracy) | Takedown Defense: 0% Current Ranking: No. 13 | Last fight: Technical knockout win over Justin Tafa Derrick Lewis has the most knockouts in the history of UFC and that’s probably the best thing you can say about the “Black Beast” in terms of his MMA career. To be fair, the 40 year-old Texan also has eight post-fight performance bonuses with three “Fight of the Night” honors, leaving him just one shy of the division mark set by former heavyweight champion, Stipe Miocic. Lewis has been competing for UFC since his technical knockout win over Jack May back in early 2014, a span of more than 11 years (Lewis was just 29 at the time of his debut). In the years that followed, “Mattress Mack’s” favorite customer compiled a record of 19-10 with one No Contest and he currently sits just inside the Top 10 at 265 pounds. Lewis has been dealing with a bad back for most of his career and has pretty much mailed it in for the last several years. “Black Beast” is coming off a technical knockout victory over Rodrigo Nascimento but has lost five of his last eight, getting finished in four of those losses. In fact, nine of his 12 losses have come by way of knockout or submission — but Lewis is rarely in a boring fight (this abomination notwithstanding). “I’ve fought way more tough fighters than this guy,” Lewis told UFC.com. “All his wins just came against guys that were 0-1, 1-2, 1-1, really having no experience. So they’re really trying to build this guy up for failure. That’s what I believe. I believe it’s too soon for him. That’s what I think. I believe there really are levels to it.” “I think coming up against a guy like me, very unpredictable, very dangerous, you never know what to expect,” Lewis continued. “I think it’s just too early for him to fight someone like me. He should expect that [I’m] going to come at him like no other opponent has come at him before. He’s going to realize that he made a big mistake signing that paper.” Tallison Teixeira is the new kid on the proverbial block and he’s already gotten everyone’s attention by racking up eight straight first-round knockout finishes. The Brazilian blasted his way onto the roster by popping and dropping Arthur Lopes on Dana White’s “Contender Series” back in Sept. of 2024 then followed that up with a 35-second finish over Justin Tafa at UFC 312. To earn a main event slot in just two fights for the promotion should tell you what matchmakers think of Teixeira’s skill set, or maybe they figure the aging and somewhat-brittle Lewis has declined enough to make this fight even, since they are not even remotely close in experience. Like most MMA fans, I like what I see from Teixeira and he is without question a lethal striker, Standing 6’7” with a 83-inch reach certainly helps, but not as much as fighting absolute nobodies on the international circuit. Lopes went back to the regional circuit after losing to Teixeira and Tafa is an undersized heavyweight, so I’m not sure those are the kinds of wins that should be driving “Xicao” to a -280 betting favorite. Did we already forget what happened to that other 6’7” heavyweight knockout artist who dazzled Dana White on “Contender Series” then won his first UFC fight by knockout? I’m talking about Robelis Despaigne, who went from cock of the walk to feather duster in two fights and is now fighting for those weird crypto bros under the Karate Combat banner. “I like this because I’ll be remembered as the man that ended the Brazilian curse,” Teixeira told MMA Fighting. “Brazilians need this after sad losses we had. Brazil needs this incentive, you know? I think that motivates me even more to give my best possible [performance] inside the Octagon.” Lewis is not without his issues and you can never quite tell if he actually gives a s—t about his fighting career or just wants to collect his paycheck and go home. What I can say for certain, is that he’s fought (and defeated) some of the best heavyweights in the world and also stopped heavyweights taller than Teixeira, like Alexander Volkov. Unless “The Black Beast” is completely washed (or completely checked out), I think he shows the 25 year-old hotshot there are levels to this game, even when some of the playing pieces are old and cracked. Prediction: Lewis def. Teixeira by knockout 170 lbs.: Stephen Thompson vs. Gabriel Bonfim Stephen “Wonderboy” Thompson Record: 17-8-1 | Age: 42 | Betting line: +320 Wins: 8 KO/TKO, 1 SUB, 8 DEC | Losses: 2 KO/TKO, 1 SUB, 5 DEC Height: 6’0“ | Reach: 75” | Stance: Orthodox Significant Strikes Landed Per Minute: 4.11 | Striking accuracy: 46% Strikes Absorbed Per Minute: 3.02 | Striking Defense: 55% Takedown Average: 0.25 (41% accuracy) | Takedown Defense: 63% Current Ranking: No. 12 | Last fight: Knockout loss to Joaquin Buckley Gabriel “Marretinha” Bonfim Record: 17-1 | Age: 27 | Betting line: -410 Wins: 3 KO/TKO, 13 SUB, 1 DEC | Losses: 1 KO/TKO, 0 SUB, 0 DEC Height: 6’1“ | Reach: 72” | Stance: Orthodox Significant Strikes Landed Per Minute: 5.22 | Striking accuracy: 43% Strikes Absorbed Per Minute: 3.80 | Striking Defense: 65% Takedown Average: 3.68 (76% accuracy) | Takedown Defense: 73% Current Ranking: Unranked | Last fight: Submission win over Kalinn Williams Stephen Thompson is 42 years old, has lost four of his last five, and is coming off a brutal knockout loss to Joaquin Buckley at UFC 307 last October. In fact, “Wonderboy” has just four wins over the last nine years but somehow retained his spot in the division Top 15, sandwiched between Geoff Neal and Carlos Prates. Thompson is a former kickboxer and continues to fight like one, getting taken down 17 times across his last five fights. I’m not sure what the former welterweight title challenger has left to offer at this point in his combat sports career, but trying to stay off the ground and outpoint fighters for a decision has not been a winning strategy and Thompson is facing an opponent who averages more than three takedowns per fight. “I’ve got two fights left, and we’re going to see them through, we’re going to honor them,” Thompson told MMA Junkie. “Go out there and win these next two fights in a great fashion, and we’ll see if we’ll keep going. It depends on what the UFC wants to do for sure. God forbid, if it doesn’t, then I’ve got other routes that I can take.” “I’m notorious for giving these guys a shot,” Thompson continued. “I did it with Vicente Luque, Geoff Neal, Kevin Holland. I’m just the guy to allow these guys to come up and test themselves. I wouldn’t be where I am if it wasn’t for those guys — Jake Ellenberger, Johny Hendricks, Rory MacDonald. Those guys gave me a shot. So just giving these guys a chance to prove themselves coming up, that’s kind of what it is at this point.” Gabriel Bonfim cut his teeth on Dana White’s “Contender Series” back in late 2022 and outside of his misstep against Nicholas Dalby the following year — when Bonfim was just 25 years old — the Brazilian has been virtually unstoppable, racking up four wins with three nasty finishes, two coming in the very first round. “Marretinha” may not be in his fighting prime just yet but he’s pretty damn close and already looks like a future title contender, though you can also argue that Bonfim has yet to fight an elite welterweight. I doubt anyone is breaking out the party hats for victories over Kalinn Williams and Ange Loosa. Stylistically, this is simply a bad matchup for Thompson, who thrives when opponents afford him the space to strike from range, like Kevin Holland. Despite his numerous submissions, Bonfim is no slouch on his feet and will be able to keep “Wonderboy” in reverse with his constant aggression. That should lead to some tie-ups against the cage and eventually, the takedown. Thompson has only been submitted once in his professional MMA career, though it’s probably because he’s never fought a black belt in Brazilian Jiu Jitsu with the credentials of Bonfim. I don’t want to harp on the age difference here (it’s 15 years if you’re counting) so I will instead harp on the fact that Thompson continues to look worse in each successive fight. text: Stephen “Wonderboy” Thompson returns to action on July 12, 2025, at the Bridgestone Arena in Nashville, Tennessee, facing unbeaten Brazilian Gabriel Bonfim. It’s a compelling clash of styles: Thompson’s veteran striking and range control versus Bonfim’s youthful power and submission skill. With contrasting career trajectories and skill sets, this matchup could turn on simple physics—who can impose their game plan first. Thompson’s takedown defense and footwork can frustrate and neutralize less disciplined pressure. If Thompson stays light on his feet and lands crisp counters, he’s likely to frustrate Bonfim out of his rhythm and gradually take control. The veteran’s timing and accuracy should enable him to catch Bonfim charging in with a clean shot. Thompson’s experience and movement advantage are key. title: UFC Nashville odds: Best betting props, parlays and picks | Lewis vs. Teixeira
text: UFC Nashville goes down this weekend (Sat., July 12, 2025) inside Bridgestone Arena in Nashville, Tennessee. The main event features Heavyweights with Derrick Lewis vs. Tallison Teixeira. Lewis, a divisional stalwart, is hoping to get past the UFC neophyte and secure a fight with new UFC champion, Tom Aspinall. When it comes to the rest of the UFC Nashville card, there’s not too much to write home about. The co-main is Stephen Thompson vs. Gabriel Bonfim. Rounding out the main card is Calvin Kattar vs. Steve Garcia, Nate Landwehr vs. Morgan Charriere, Vitor Petrino vs. Austin Lane and Junior Tafa vs Tuco Tokkos. UFC Nashville’s “Prelims” are headlined by Max Griffin vs. Chris Curtis. The “Prelims” also have Jake Matthews vs. Chidi Njokuani and Lauren Murphy vs. Eduarda Moura. As always, there’s lots to bet on this card and we’ve got odds for all the fights below: UFC Nashville Main Card Money Line Odds Derrick Lewis (+220) vs. Tallison Teixeira (-270) The towering Teixeira is just 8-0 and two fights into his UFC career. He debuted in the Octagon with a Contender Series first round knockout over Arthur Lopes. In his proper debut, he put away Justin Tafa in 35 seconds (see it here). Lewis — who turned 40 this year — is coming off a third round technical knockout win over Rodrigo Nascimento. Before that, he lost a five-round decision to Jailton Almeida. And before that, he scored a 33-second win over Marcos Rogerio Lima (see it here). That win snapped a three fight losing skid (all finishes) where he lost to Serghei Spivac, Sergei Pavlovich and Tai Tuivasa. There’s not much to scout when it comes to Teixeira. He’s very tall and very long and he’s coming into UFC in his athletic prime at only 25 years-old. Lewis is giving up four inches of height and four inches of reach to the young Brazilian. The last time Lewis fought someone with that kind of reach it was Pavlovich and he lasted just 55 seconds. Lewis is capable of the spectacular and shocking in an Octagon. But, it really feels like the odds are stacked against him here, with a fighter so long, so powerful and with so much youth on his side. Lewis’ defense against significant strikes is just 40 percent. That spells a lot of trouble for “The Black Beast” against a man who, so far, has landed 14.61 significant strikes per-minute across his three Octagon appearances. In Heavyweight, it only takes one punch to win, a lot of the times, but I have to favor the man who is going to be landing dozens of them in a round (if it makes it that far). The round total for this fight is set at 1.5. I think the under is most likely, as do many others. The odds are just -210 for that prop. Teixeira by KO/TKO/DQ is a laughable -185. And Teixeira to win by strikes in round one is just -125. Clearly, there’s not much value if you believe Teixeira is going to quickly separate Lewis from his consciousness (as I do). For my best bet, I’m going to go for a winning round and method of victory parlay. I’m taking round one and TKO/KO/DQ. This covers me just in case Lewis does something silly/outstanding in the first round in Nashville. Best bet: Fight to end in Round 1 by KO/TKO/DQ (-150) Stephen Thompson (+320) vs. Gabriel Bonfim (-410) Thompson is coming off a third round knockout loss to Joaquin Buckley (see it here). Before that, he was submitted by Shavkat Rakhmonov (see it here). His last win was over Kevin Holland, when Holland retired at the end of round four. Bonfim, on the other hand, choked out Khaos Williams in his last fight (see it here). Before that, he took a decision over Ange Loosa. Before those fights he lost, as a big favorite, to Nicolas Dalby via technical knockout (see it here). I don’t think Thompson is long for this sport. He turned 42 this year and his fighting style isn’t great for masking your age. He can’t hide behind takedowns and take dangerous finishers out of their comfort zones. He has to stand in front of them and hope he can slip strikes and land enough from range to earn a decision. Bonfim is not a dangerous striker, so I’m not worried about Thompson getting KO’d for the second time in two fights. Bonfim’s submission threat is what I’m worried about, though. Bonfim’s submissions come from all angles and at a scary pace. I don’t think Thompson will be able to fight those off for long enough to stay in the fight and will probably end up tapping from a choke. Thompson has never had elite takedown defense. With age, his 63 percent takedown defense will feel closer to 50 percent. Bonfim lands almost four takedowns per 15 minutes. He’s going to get Thompson down. Bonfim by submission is only +125. I feel strongly that this is what’s going to happen. But those odds are a little stingy. Unfortunately, the Bonfim -3.5 is even stingier at -205. For my best bet I’m going deep into DraftKings props and I’m looking at Bonfim to win in rounds one or two. I really struggle to see Thompson make it to the final bell and this at least covers me if Thompson is shot to the point that Bonfim can get him out of there with ground-and-pound. Best bet: Gabriel Bonfim to win in rounds 1-2 (+120) Calvin Kattar (+102) vs. Steve Garcia (-122) The Featherweight division have a right to be scared of Garcia. He’s one a five-fight finish streak right now, including stoppages over Melquizael Costa (see it here) and Chase Hooper (see it here). Hooper and Costa have looked pretty good since then, so that tells us what kind of level Costa has been operating at lately. Kattar, on the other hand, will lock up a rare five-fight losing streak in UFC if he gets stopped by Garcia. Last time out he was well beaten by Youssef Zalal (who won despite staying in cruise control). Before that, he was beaten by Aljamain Sterling, Arnold Allen (due to an injury) and Josh Emmett (split decision). Kattar’s toughness is the stuff of legend, thanks to the unholy beating he once took from Max Holloway. Kattar has never been stopped in his career (other than that knee injury). At 37, though, with all these wars in his past, is this the time we see that chin fade? I think so. Garcia’s punches land like a sock full of pennies. And I fear he’s going to land something really hard on Kattar. I think we’re going to see a technical knockout from Garcia, probably from ground-and-pound. I’ll take the point spread here on Garcia, believing that if Kattar doesn’t go down, Garcia will still take a dominant decision (also because Garcia by KO was only +165). Best bet: Steve Garcia -3.5 (+110) Nate Landwehr (+220) vs. Morgan Charriere (-270) Landwehr got styled on in his last fight. Doo Ho Choi looked incredible as he out-struck and out-wrestled and eventually finished “The Train” (see it here). Before that, Landwehr scored a comeback technical knockout on Jamall Emmers (see it here). In his early UFC career, Landwehr managed to get wins over Darren Elkins, L’udovit Klein and David Onama. Charriere, meanwhile, is coming off a unanimous decision loss to Nathaniel Wood where he looked good, not great. Before that, he blew away Gabriel Miranda with a left hook (see it here). Landwehr is a hard-nosed brawler who is willing to eat two shot to land one. He’s a bit like Elkins without the grappling (as exposed by how often Choi took and held him down). I think this is a very tough match-up for him, against Charriere who has looked good against opponents who charge at him. Both these guys absorb more significant strikes than they land (which is a big red flag for me), but Charriere’s negative differential is higher. Charriere is also giving up three inches in the reach department. Even so, I think Charriere’s counter punching will be the story of this fight. Landwehr doesn’t exactly fight behind his jab and pick his shots. He’ll be crashing forward trying to overwhelm Charriere. In this situation, I like Charriere to respond with something hard that puts Landwehr down. Charriere reminds me of a striker in football/soccer who misses the goal when he’s given too much time to think about his shot, but who can score on instinct when the ball comes to him and he has to react without thinking. That’s how I see Charriere getting his finish here. Best bet: Morgan Charriere moneyline (-220) Vitor Petrino (-700) vs. Austen Lane (+500) Petrino’s shiny 11-0 record was dulled by Anthony Smith and Dustin Jacoby last year. Smith scored a quick guillotine on the Brazilian (see it here) in Brazil. Then Jacoby scored a late knockout in a very boring fight (see it here). Lane, meanwhile, was KO’d by Mario Pinto last time out (see it here). Before that, he successfully fraud checked Robelis Despaigne. Prior to that fight, he was starched by Jhonata Diniz (see it here). If it wasn’t for Tuco Tokkos, Lane might be the worst fighter on a UFC main card this year. Lane has a terrible 40 percent defense on significant strikes. That’s a death sentence at Heavyweight. For the most part in his career, big shots have been able to find Lane and he’s been stopped more than your average bear (all six of his defeats are by knockout). He’s been stopped so much, that you wonder whether the 37 year old should still get a license. But, this is MMA, right? We’ll let anyone fight. Petrino came to UFC with a reputation for vicious striking, but we’ve not seen much of that in the Octagon. What we have seen has been pretty slow and telegraphed. Is that still too fast and unpredictable for Lane, though? Lane has a decent-size advantage against Petrino and I can actually see him taking Petrino down and laying on him for a round or two. However, whenever they are standing I’m worried that Lane is one punch away from being laid out. This is what we saw in the Diniz fight. Since they start rounds standing, I have to give this to Petrino. I’m not very enthusiastic about the pick, though. The round total is 1.5. I’ll go with the over, thinking Lane will get his early takedown and Petrino will continue to underwhelm, even in a winning effort. Best bet: Over 1.5 rounds (+135) Junior Tafa (-166) vs. Tuco Tokkos (+140) Tafa put away super short notice opponent Sean Sharaf back in Oct. 2024. That was his first fight since being heel hooked by Valter Walker (who fights further down the card). Before that, Tafa was TKO’d by Marcos Rogerio de Lima (see it here). Tokkos, meanwhile, stifled Navajo Stirling last time out, losing just by decision to the super hyped prospect. Before that he was submitted by Oumar Sy, with Sy locking up the rear-naked choke when Tokkos was mugging for the commentary booth. Tokkos, as referenced earlier, is probably the worst main card fighter of the year. He’s not shown us much of anything thus far in his UFC career. He did well to hang in there against Stirling, but he offered very little offensive threat. Stirling’s passivity was mostly to blame for that awful fight going the distance. Tafa isn’t much better. He’s 2-3 in UFC and the two guys he beat are well below UFC quality. I think Tafa wins this, thanks to how hittable Tokkos is (4.99 significant strikes absorbed per minute and just 33 percent significant strike defense). I wouldn’t be surprised if we get another stinker, though, that goes the distance with a decision that could go to either guy. Because I’m not sold on Tafa, over 1.5 rounds looks quite appealing. Best bet: Over 1.5 rounds (+105) UFC Nashville ‘Prelims’ Under Card Odds Max Griffin (+250) vs. Chris Curtis (-310) This is our featured “Prelim”? I guess this slot really is just, “the fight before the main card” now. The 39-year-old Griffin was tapped by Michael Chiesa in Dec. 2024. He’s been win-loss-win-loss for the past few years, with the wins being split decisions over Jeremiah Wells and Tim Means. The 37-year-old Curtis is coming off trying to separate Sean Strickland from some dude in a regional MMA cage. In his last UFC fight, Curtis lost a controversial fight with Roman Kopylov (see it here). That fight was officially ruled a head kick knockout loss at 4:59 of round three. Many felt the fight could have been left for the remaining second and then have the judges decide (I scored it for Kopylov anyways). Griffin is an okay striker and wrestler, but at 39, his potency in either area needs to be questioned. Curtis, who isn’t much younger, seems to still be a reliable and creative volume striker. His very good takedown defense probably holds up to the level needed to stay up against Griffin, too. I think there’s a chance Curtis gets a stoppage in this fight, but it might come late. I’m not going to mess around with any round betting here and instead just go with Curtis on the moneyline. Best bet: Chris Curtis moneyline (-310) Jake Matthews (+124) vs. Chidi Njokuani (-148) Both these guys are on good runs and coming off decisive wins. It’s a little surprising to see them matched up here on the “Prelims.” Matthews beat Francisco Prado by unanimous decision in February. Last year, he defeated Phil Rowe. Prior to that, he managed to make it to a losing decision against the undefeated Michael Morales. Njokuani, meanwhile, lit up Elizeu Zaleski dos Santos on the co-main of an APEX card in March (see it here). He did miss weight for that one, though. Prior to that TKO he beat Jared Gooden and Rhys McKee. Njokuani is very big for the weight class. He’s four inches taller than Matthews and will have a long seven-inch reach advantage. That reach could be significant, as it was in Njokuani’s destruction of Dos Santos. Njokuani’s reach gets even more deadlier when you consider he has the best accuracy rate for sig. strikes in the division at 62 percent. The only reason he isn’t the official leader in that stat at Welterweight is because his last two fights have technically been Catchweights (due to his weigh-in misses). The 62 percent is better than Gunnar Nelson’s official best mark of 60.6 percent and all the other killers in this rejuvenated weight class. Matthews is no slouch, though. He’s an intelligent and well rounded fighter. He probably knows he can’t win a kickboxing match and I think he’s going to try and make this an ugly brawl against the fence. He’ll look to grind on Njokuani and land a few takedowns. That might be tough, though, given Njokuani’s 75 percent takedown defense. Ultimately, I think Njokuani is going to prevent himself getting taken down in this fight. And, if Matthews, won’t let him strike from range, I still think Njokuani has a good shot at landing heavy strikes right inside Matthews’ kitchen. Njokuani’s Muay Thai style is perfect for clinch fighting, so he might find a home for some good elbows and knees. The round total for this one is set at 1.5 for some reason. The over on that is -298, so no value there. And I don’t think there’s a finish in this fight. I’ll just go with the Njokuani moneyline. Best bet: Chidi Njokuani moneyline (-148) Lauren Murphy (+440) vs. Eduarda Moura (-600) Murphy has been out of action since her bruising loss to Jessica Andrade in Jan. 2023. Before that, she dominated the un-retired Miesha Tate. Before those fights, she was TKO’d while trying to get the belt off Valentina Shevchenko. Moura, meanwhile, took a decision over Veronica Hardy in her Flyweight debut last year. That fight came after she misses weight in back-to-back Strawweight bouts. I get that Murphy has been out awhile, and that she’s 42, but Vegas is showing a lot of faith in Moura with these lines. Despite her age and inactivity as of late, I bet Murphy still “has that dog in her” and I think she will bring a lot of pressure to Moura. Moura has managed to package together wins thanks to her takedowns. Murphy’s takedown defense has been solid over her career (69 percent). The big question is whether Murphy still has good takedown defense or not. If she keeps this fight standing I think she has a good chance to take a close decision. If she is taken down, I think Moura should be able to keep her down and get a pretty comfortable decision. Either way, I think we’re going to decision. Best bet: Over 2.5 rounds (-330) Kennedy Nzechukwu (-205) vs. Valter Walker (+170) Nzechukwu is undefeated (2-0) in UFC’s Heavyweight division. In Dec. 2024, he scored a first round technical knockout over Lukasz Brzeski (see it here). Walker, on the other hand, lost to Brzeski, by decision, in his UFC debut. Since then he’s heel hooked both Junior Tafa (who didn’t like it one bit) and Don’Tale Mayes. Nzechukwu’s striking should be too much for Walker to handle. However, Nzechukwu is a little ungainly and I can totally see him getting caught by Walker’s leg locks, perhaps even after scoring a knockdown. This match-up really seems ripe for some Heavyweight nuttiness. I think it’s best to play the under in this situation, especially with the round total set at 2.5 (I was sure it would be 1.5). Best bet: Under 2.5 rounds (-105) Mitch Ramirez (+700) vs. Mike Davis (-1000) Ramirez was stopped by Thiago Moises leg kicks in his last fight (see those here). His only other Octagon appearance was a walloping from Carlos Prates on Contender Series. In the opposite corner, Davis returned from a year long lay-off to fight Fares Ziam in February. He looked out of sorts and was possibly carrying an injury in that fight. He seemed to be trying to minimize damage more so than win a fight. That unanimous decision was his first UFC loss since being submitted by Gilbert Burns in 2019. He’s won four UFC fights between those losses. If the Davis we’re used to seeing shows up, then he should win this without too much trouble (as reflected in those betting lines). I think we’ll see the good version of Davis in this fight and if that happens, then his funky grappling should lead to a convincing win, probably by stoppage. Best bet: Under 2.5 rounds (-180) Fatima Kline (-1200) vs. Melissa Martinez (+750) Kline was fed to the wolves on her UFC debut, coming in on short notice and up a weight class to take on Jasmine Jasudavicius. She got dominated by the bigger fighter in that bout, but rebounded with a technical knockout over Victoria Dudakova (see it here). Prior to joining UFC, Kline was a champ in the CFFC organization. She also has BJJ black belt under Mike Wacker. Martinez, meanwhile, is 1-1 in UFC with a decision win over Alice Ardelean and a decision loss to Elise Reed. She’s a former champ in the Combate organization. Martinez — who is just 5’2” — should be fighting at Atomweight (and UFC should have an Atomweight division). Kline is going to have a lot of size and strength over her (not much reach, though). I think that size difference will be most notable on the ground and I think Kline is going to use that to get a submission. Best bet: Under 2.5 rounds (+114) UFC Nashville Long Shots! Here’s a couple of long shots for Saturday night’s action. Derrick Lewis to Win and Over 3.5 (+1000) Let’s just imagine that Teixeira is being over-hyped and that his best work has all come against tomato cans. And let’s imagine that Lewis is going to rewind the clock and survive a lot of early punishment. Maybe Teixeira punches himself out? And then, maybe Lewis uncorks one of his classic right hooks that knocks him out cold? It’s not impossible, right? It’s Heavyweight after all. Three-fight parlay: Tallison Teixeira, Steve Garcia, Valter Walker (+568) Despite that first long shot bet, I’m reasonably confident that Teixeira is legit enough to be better than a 40-year-old Lewis. I’m also pretty confident that Steve Garcia will add to his impressive winning streak when he meets Kattar. Walker is my wild card in this parlay and he’s here to add some value. Nzechukwu has looked good at Heavyweight so far, but he’s not faced anyone like Walker.
